1	# Native flex layouts (opt-in)
2	
3	By default every board the importer creates is a fixed snapshot of the viewport:
4	each layer sits at the position the browser measured, so the result matches the
5	page but does not respond when you edit it. **Native flex layouts** is an opt-in
6	setting (Advanced capture, off by default) that turns simple flex containers
7	into Penpot flex boards, so resizing the board, resizing a child, or adding a
8	layer reflows its children. Anything the conversion cannot reproduce exactly
9	stays a fixed snapshot. Nothing about the default import changes.
10	
11	Status: unit, fixture, and importer regressions are checked in, and a live
12	Penpot pass covers geometry at all three viewports, resizing and editing,
13	undo/redo, and a saved reload; see [Verification](#verification). The text box,
14	fill, wrap, and reverse additions (#49) have their own live pass on Penpot
15	2.18.4, which also found that Penpot justifies reversed layouts on the physical
16	axis and wraps a reversed sequence differently from CSS.
17	
18	## How a container is chosen
19	
20	The conversion is decided in two stages, both against the same small model
21	(`predictFlex` in `src/importer/flexLayout.ts`) of how a flex container places
22	its children: lines broken in source order, free space distributed by
23	`justify-content` and `align-content`, reversed axes mirrored, growing items
24	sharing the free space equally, and each layer inset in its item by a margin.
25	
26	1. **Before import (browser snapshot).** A container qualifies only when the
27	   model, fed the browser's own child sizes, reproduces the browser's child
28	   positions and sizes within 1 px. Margins, `order`, auto margins, and
29	   anything else the model cannot express fail this check on their own, so
30	   unsupported CSS cannot silently shift layers.
31	2. **After import (host check).** Penpot applies a layout asynchronously, and in
32	   live passes the first layout on a freshly opened page did not run at all.
33	   The importer therefore piles the children at the board origin before adding
34	   the layout, waits for the host to settle, and requires the host's positions
35	   to match the model fed the host's current sizes. A layout that never ran, or
36	   ran differently, is removed and the children return to their captured
37	   offsets, with a `NATIVE_LAYOUT_REVERTED` diagnostic.
38	
39	Text may reflow in Penpot's substituted font, which is why the host check uses
40	the host's sizes rather than the browser's.
41	
42	## Supported subset
43	
44	| CSS | Penpot |
45	| --- | --- |
46	| `display: flex` / `inline-flex`, `flex-direction: row`, `column`, `row-reverse`, or `column-reverse` | A board with a flex layout of the same direction. Penpot reverses only the order and keeps justification on the physical axis, so a reversed container's justification is mirrored (CSS `flex-start` becomes Penpot `end`). CSS `start` and `end` follow the writing mode and need no mirroring. |
47	| `flex-wrap: wrap` (not reversed) | Wrap, with `align-content` (`normal`/`stretch`, `flex-start`, `center`, `flex-end`, and the `space-*` values) as the matching line alignment. Centered or spaced lines must fit. |
48	| `gap` | The main-axis gap between items and the cross-axis gap between lines. |
49	| `padding` (plus a uniform border) | Board padding. A uniform border is a native inside stroke and does not move children, so its width is added to the padding. |
50	| `justify-content`: `flex-start`, `center`, `flex-end`, `space-between`, `space-around`, `space-evenly` | The matching justification. Centering and spacing require the children to fit. |
51	| `align-items`: `flex-start`, `center`, `flex-end`, and the default `stretch` | Start, center, end. Captured children already have their stretched size, so start alignment reproduces `stretch`. |
52	| Text items | The element box, not the glyph line: the inset of the glyphs in the box becomes the text layer's margins. |
53	| `flex-grow` | `fill` sizing along the main axis when the browser shared the free space equally (for example `flex: 1` siblings or a single growing item). Otherwise the item keeps its captured size. |
54	| Absolutely positioned children | Flagged as outside the flow and kept at their captured offset. They are appended first so they stay topmost. |
55	| Nested flex containers | Each converts on its own merits. |
56	| Fill, border, radius, shadow, opacity, background image | Painted by the board as for any container. |
57

59	its captured size: there is no hug, cross-axis stretch, or `flex-shrink`
60	conversion. The capture records `flex-grow`, `flex-shrink`, and `flex-basis` for
61	every element; a shrunk item already has its shrunk size in the snapshot, and an

## Real-page trial (#51)

The fixtures show that the conversion is exact. They do not show how much of a
real page it reaches, or what keeps the rest fixed. On 2026-10-24, twelve public
pages were run through the production plugin UI, and the scenes it would post
to Penpot were tallied with the importer's own planner (`planSceneFlex`):

```sh
npm run build && npx vite preview --port 4173 --strictPort &
node scripts/importer-native-trial.mjs <output-dir>   # capture + analyze
node scripts/importer-native-trial.mjs <output-dir> analyze
```

The script loads the real UI in headless Chrome, inside a same-origin frame so
the UI is not standalone. It enters each URL, analyzes at the three default
viewports with scripts off, presses Import, and keeps the `IMPORT` message's
scenes. Stripe and Linear exceeded the UI's 30-second analysis deadline at three
viewports and are not counted.

| Page | Kind | Flex containers (desktop / tablet / mobile) | Converted |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| vite.dev | landing | 90 / 65 / 62 | 61% / 52% / 55% |
| tailwindcss.com | landing | 145 / 144 / 139 | 68% / 65% / 67% |
| github.com | landing | 145 / 137 / 137 | 67% / 70% / 71% |
| Bootstrap dashboard example | dashboard | 24 / 24 / 8 | 79% / 71% / 50% |
| Bootstrap pricing example | dashboard | 9 / 9 / 9 | 56% each |
| MDN `flex` reference | docs | 160 / 32 / 32 | 12% / 56% / 56% |
| docs.python.org | docs | 5 / 6 / 6 | 40% / 50% / 50% |
| Vite guide | docs | 106 / 21 / 18 | 89% / 71% / 72% |
| Bootstrap cheatsheet | components | 115 / 109 / 109 | 38% / 41% / 44% |
| ui.shadcn.com | components | 220 / 142 / 17 | 88% / 84% / 76% |

Overall, **1,400 of 2,245 flex containers (62%) convert**: 698 of 1,064 on
landing pages, 55 of 83 on dashboards, 185 of 386 in docs, and 462 of 712 in
component libraries. Of the converted containers, 522 hold text items, 131
use `fill`, 90 wrap, and none are reversed. The same pages have 375 grid
containers, which are never converted.

The 845 containers kept fixed, by reason:

| Kept fixed because | Containers | Share of kept |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Child positions do not match the model | 397 | 47% |
| In-flow children differ in stacking | 147 | 17% |
| Per-side borders | 142 | 17% |
| No in-flow children (nothing to lay out) | 73 | 9% |
| Positioned flow children beside absolute ones | 37 | 4% |
| A text line overflows its element's box | 29 | 3% |
| A rotated child | 15 | 2% |
| Centered or spaced children overflow | 4 | <1% |
| `align-items: baseline` | 1 | <1% |

The mismatch bucket was split by geometry: 239 have uneven main-axis spacing
from item margins (often a `::before` icon with a right margin), 54 have one
auto margin pushing items to the far end, 14 start with a leading margin, 31
plus 4 are offset on the cross axis, 21 are wrapped lines, 16 overflow the main
axis, 4 are reordered with `order`, and 14 are unclassified. **Item margins,
auto margins included, account for about 307 of the 845 kept containers**:
the capture records margins only for text items, through their element box.

Nine of those scenes were imported into Penpot 2.18.4-RC5 through Orca's

harness takes the captured scenes with
`PHASE5_SCENES=<scenes.json> node scripts/importer-live-harness.mjs`.
`compare <snapshotPage> <nativePage>` pairs every layer by viewport, source,
and type (nearest first when several layers share a source, as border sides
and text runs do) and counts those that moved or resized by more than 1 px.
Groups are counted separately, since a group draws nothing itself.
`reflow-probe <page>` grows every native board 40 px along its main axis,
checks that the host's child positions match the model at the new size,
restores the size, and checks again.

**The trial found a conversion defect.** The first Bootstrap dashboard import
converted 19 containers, reverted none, and moved 381 layers 24 px left. The
sidebar-and-content row has the padded `<main>` as a flex item. An undecorated
container is imported as a group, or collapsed onto its single child, and a
group's bounds shrink to its content. Penpot's layout then places those
bounds, not the element box, at the item's slot, so the padding vanished. The
host check missed it because it predicts from the host's own layer sizes. Two
changes fix it:

- A container laid out by a native flex board is imported as a non-clipping
  board at its element box, as the flex board itself is (the `#padded-item`
  fixture tile).
- The host check also requires every non-text, non-filling layer to keep its
  captured size, so a layer whose bounds are not its item (an SVG drawn inside
  its viewport, say) reverts its container instead of moving.
